html:
Who we are

Ecobraz Emigre is the Associação Auxílio à Reciclagem de Eletrônicos e Inclusão Digital – Ecobraz, registered under CNPJ 14.197.457/0001-42 and headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil. The organisation collects, sorts, processes and forwards electrical and electronic waste, and also develops reuse and digital inclusion initiatives.

What we do

  • Electronic waste collection for companies, institutions and individuals, subject to assessment;
  • Reverse logistics and recurring operations;
  • Decommissioning of IT assets and electronic equipment;
  • Treatment of media and data within the contracted scope;
  • Traceability and documentation appropriate to the operation;
  • Responsible reuse where technically and operationally applicable.

How we work

Each request is assessed on the basis of material, quantity, location, access, risks, logistics and the evidence required. Submitting a request does not automatically confirm collection: our team validates feasibility and conditions before scheduling.

Institutional identification

  • Legal name: Associação Auxílio à Reciclagem de Eletrônicos e Inclusão Digital – Ecobraz;
  • CNPJ (Brazilian company register): 14.197.457/0001-42;
  • Address: Rua Dona Maria Quedas, 230, Jardim Andaraí, São Paulo/SP, Brazil, postcode 02175-010;
  • Telephone: +55 11 4329-2001;
  • Email: contato@ecobraz.org.br.

Commitment to verifiable information

Capabilities, documents and commercial conditions must correspond to the service actually contracted and performed. For this reason, Ecobraz avoids generic promises and records limits, responsibilities and deliverables within the scope of each operation.

html:
Air conditioners should not be treated as ordinary scrap

Climate control units may contain refrigerant fluid, oil, a compressor, circuit boards and metals. De-installation, refrigerant recovery and physical removal are distinct stages and must be declared in the scope.

Equipment we assess

  • Split systems, condensing and evaporator units;
  • Window and portable units;
  • Evaporative coolers, water dispensers and related equipment;
  • Corporate lots arising from refurbishments and decommissioning projects.

Before you enquire

Let us know whether the equipment is still installed or has already been removed, who carried out the refrigerant recovery, plus the model, capacity, quantity, photographs and site access. Do not cut pipework or release refrigerant into the atmosphere.

Frequently asked questions

Does Ecobraz carry out de-installation?

This requirement must be flagged for assessment. Collection of equipment that has already been de-installed does not automatically include specialist HVAC services.

Where can I dispose of an old air conditioner?

The solution depends on your location and the condition of the unit. Send us the details for assessment.

title: Battery and UPS disposal
custom_excerpt: Collection of lithium, lead-acid, stationary, traction, automotive and electric-vehicle batteries, plus UPS units — with technical assessment and documentation.
meta_title: Battery & UPS Disposal | Documented Collection | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request collection of lithium, lead-acid, stationary, traction, automotive and EV batteries, plus UPS units, with technical assessment and documentation.
html:
Battery collection with proper handling, transport and final destination

Batteries call for packaging, transport and final treatment that meet specific requirements — and that is precisely the flow Ecobraz organises. Each collection is defined by a technical assessment of type, quantity, condition (including damaged or swollen units), location and the documentation required.

Battery types we collect

  • Lithium batteries (equipment, power tools, corporate power banks);
  • Lead-acid batteries;
  • Stationary batteries (UPS systems, telecoms, energy banks);
  • Traction and forklift batteries;
  • Automotive batteries — cars, motorcycles and fleets;
  • Marine and railway batteries;
  • Batteries from e-bikes, e-scooters and other light electric vehicles.

Please note: loose household batteries (AA, AAA and similar) are not accepted — for these, please use the official retail and manufacturer reverse-logistics collection points.

UPS units and voltage stabilisers

UPS units and voltage stabilisers are collected together with their internal batteries, within the same assessment flow. Data centre and telecoms battery banks may require an inventory, scheduled dismantling and a chain of custody — describe your scenario in the request.

How it works

  1. You describe the battery type, approximate quantity, condition and address;
  2. Our team assesses risks, packaging, logistics and the applicable documents;
  3. The scope is approved — conditions, responsibilities and timelines are defined before removal;
  4. Collection, transport and final destination follow the agreed scope, with the contracted evidence (such as the MTR waste manifest and the CDF final-destination certificate, according to the service performed).

Frequently asked questions

Do you collect car and motorcycle batteries?

Yes. Automotive batteries go through the standard collection assessment, including batches from workshops and fleets.

Do you collect forklift batteries or stationary battery banks?

Yes. Traction and stationary batteries are handled subject to an assessment of weight, access and on-site handling.

Can a swollen or damaged lithium battery be collected?

Describe its condition in your request: damaged units require specific packaging, defined during the technical assessment before removal.

Do you collect ordinary household batteries?

No. Loose household batteries should be taken to the official retail and manufacturer reverse-logistics collection points.

Which documents are issued?

Documentation varies according to the material, the transport and the contracted scope — let us know in your request what your audit process requires.

Contact us to arrange battery collection

title: Business e-waste collection
custom_excerpt: Business collection of electronics, IT assets and decommissioned equipment with planning, traceability and scope-based documentation.
meta_title: Business e-waste collection | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request business collection of electronics and IT assets. Inventory assessment, data handling, logistics, chain of custody and documentation.
html:
A business collection starts before the pick-up

Organisations need to reconcile logistics, asset control, information security, material risks and documentation. Ecobraz receives the initial details and structures the assessment according to the batch and the operation.

Corporate assets we handle

  • Computers, laptops, monitors and peripherals;
  • Servers, storage, networking, racks and media;
  • Printers, mobile phones, batteries and UPS units;
  • Electronic hospital equipment;
  • White goods, climate-control units and machinery with embedded electronics.

Information that speeds up the proposal

  • Spreadsheet or estimate of items and quantities;
  • Address, access, loading dock, lift and time window;
  • Photos and condition of the equipment;
  • Inventory, data and evidence requirements;
  • Deadline and the on-site contact responsible for the operation.

Recurring collections and multiple sites

Organisations with continuous e-waste generation or several addresses can request an assessment of a recurring flow. Frequency, consolidation, reporting and service levels need to be defined in the scope.

Frequently asked questions

Does sending a request book a date straight away?

No. It registers your request. The team checks feasibility and confirms conditions before scheduling.

Can documentation be issued?

Yes, depending on the material, the operation and the contracted service. Let us know which document you need before the proposal.

Contact us to request a business collection

title: Cable and wire disposal and processing
custom_excerpt: Assessment of batches of electrical cables, wires, harnesses, network and telecoms cabling for collection or processing.
meta_title: Cable and Wire Disposal, Collection and Processing | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request an assessment for electrical cables, wires, network and telecoms cabling. Tell us the composition, volume, origin and purpose.
html:
Cables and wires need controlled disposal

Electrical, network and telecommunications cables combine metals, polymers and different coatings. Burning, irregular disposal or uncontrolled processing can create environmental risk and the loss of recoverable material.

Materials for assessment

  • Electrical cables and installation wiring;
  • Network, telephony and telecommunications cables;
  • Harnesses, connectors, power supplies and extension leads;
  • Surplus from construction works, refurbishments, data centres and dismantling projects;
  • Identified industrial batches.

Collection or processing

The scope may involve collection, separation or processing, depending on the composition, the volume and the client's objective. Let us know whether the batch requires raw-material return, weighing, evidence or reconciliation.

Frequently asked questions

What is the minimum quantity?

Feasibility depends on the cable type, weight, address and the service requested. Send an estimate for analysis.

Are mixed cables accepted?

Describe the materials and send photos. Composition and contamination influence the recommended route.

Contact us to request a cable and wire assessment

title: Circuit board and electronic component disposal
custom_excerpt: Collection of circuit boards, power supplies, components, parts and identified electronic scrap, with assessment of volume, origin, packaging and traceability.
meta_title: Circuit Board & Electronic Component Disposal | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request collection of circuit boards, power supplies, parts and electronic components. Service for businesses, repair shops, industry and decommissioned lots.
html:
Electronic components require batch characterisation

Circuit boards, power supplies, memory modules, processors, connectors and parts may originate from maintenance, manufacturing, technical repair or equipment dismantling. Origin, composition, the mix of materials and the presence of contamination all influence destination and logistics.

Materials for assessment

  • Motherboards, circuit boards and electronic modules;
  • Power supplies, chargers, inverters and controllers;
  • Memory modules, processors, connectors and peripherals;
  • IT, telecommunications and automation parts;
  • Batches from production, maintenance, testing or dismantled equipment.

What to tell us

Describe the origin, the component type, the estimated weight or volume and how the material is stored, and send photographs. Materials containing liquids, powders or chemical residues, or of unidentified origin, must be declared and cannot be mixed with the general batch.

Frequently asked questions

Do you collect circuit boards on their own?

Feasibility depends on quantity, location, origin and composition. Send us the details for assessment.

Do dismantled parts need to be separated?

Our team will advise on segregation after reviewing the categories and the condition of the batch.

Contact us to request an electronic component assessment

html:
Before bringing your equipment

Drop-off and collection arrangements may vary depending on the type of material, the quantity, the requester's profile and the location. To avoid an unnecessary journey, request guidance before taking equipment to any address.

How to find the right arrangement

  1. Tell us whether the request is residential, corporate or institutional.
  2. Describe the equipment and the approximate quantity.
  3. Send your postcode, city and state.
  4. Our team confirms the available arrangement: collection, guided drop-off or another applicable route.

Materials that require specific assessment

  • Fridges, freezers and equipment containing refrigerant gas;
  • Damaged, swollen or leaking batteries;
  • Hospital equipment and materials subject to decontamination;
  • Heavy machinery and large volumes;
  • Corporate assets containing data or requiring inventory control.

Frequently asked questions

Can I turn up without booking?

We do not recommend it. First confirm the arrangement, the materials accepted and the applicable opening hours.

Is collection available at my address?

Availability depends on the postcode, the material, the volume and the access conditions. Send your request for assessment.

Contact us to arrange a drop-off or request a collection

title: Computer and laptop collection
custom_excerpt: Collection of desktops, laptops, monitors, peripherals and accessories, with assessment of volume, data, logistics and documentation.
meta_title: Computer and Laptop Collection and Disposal | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request collection of computers, laptops, monitors and peripherals. Corporate service with data assessment, asset inventory and documented logistics.
html:
IT disposal for companies and institutions

Computers and laptops that are no longer in use may contain data, batteries, boards, screens and components that require specific handling. Collection should take into account the condition of the assets, the quantity, the location and any need for inventory or data protection.

Equipment we handle

  • Desktops, workstations, thin clients and laptops;
  • Monitors, keyboards, mice, power supplies and chargers;
  • Boards, memory modules, processors, cables and parts;
  • HDDs, SSDs and storage media;
  • Batches of decommissioned or damaged equipment.

Before the collection

Prepare an estimate of quantities, photos, the address and access conditions, and let us know whether the assets still contain data. For corporate batches, indicate whether you need a list by asset tag or serial number.

Data and reuse

The sanitisation or destruction method should be defined according to the media, the risk and the organisation's policy. Where reuse is possible and forms part of the scope, it should only take place after the approved data treatment has been completed.

Frequently asked questions

Do you collect a single computer?

Feasibility depends on the location and the type of service. Send your request to receive the applicable guidance.

Can I send a spreadsheet of asset tags?

Yes. The team will assess the format and the level of reconciliation required before the operation.

Contact us to arrange a computer collection

title: Corporate IT equipment disposal
custom_excerpt: Collection and treatment of IT assets, with assessment of location, volume, chain of custody, data requirements and the documentation your organisation needs.
meta_title: Corporate IT disposal and equipment collection | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request an assessment for the collection and disposal of corporate computers, laptops, servers, monitors, network equipment and other IT assets.
html:
IT assets require a dedicated disposal workflow

Computers, laptops, servers, storage arrays, switches, routers and media can hold data, credentials, controlled components and internal records. Collection should therefore begin by defining the inventory, the location, the volume and the documentation requirements.

Materials we handle

  • Computers, laptops, thin clients and workstations;
  • Monitors, peripherals, power supplies, cables and accessories;
  • Servers, storage arrays, racks and data centre equipment;
  • Switches, routers, telephony and network infrastructure;
  • HDDs, SSDs, tapes and other storage media;
  • Printers, multifunction devices and corporate electronic equipment.

How requests are assessed

  1. Scope: materials, quantities, location and access restrictions.
  2. Data: presence of storage media and any need for sanitisation or physical destruction.
  3. Logistics: packaging, removal, handling and the operational window.
  4. Records: inventory, chain of custody and documents consistent with the contracted service.

Who this service is for

Businesses, industrial sites, hospitals, schools, residential complexes, public bodies, data centres and institutions with decommissioned assets, infrastructure changes or a recurring flow of electronic equipment.

Frequently asked questions

Is collection confirmed as soon as a request is sent?

No. Each request starts a technical and logistical feasibility assessment. Our team confirms the conditions, timescales and scope before the service goes ahead.

Can equipment be listed by asset tag or serial number?

Any inventory requirement should be stated in the request. The format of the record depends on the approved scope and the service performed.

Is equipment containing data handled separately?

Yes, when this forms part of the agreed scope. Tell us the media types and security requirements involved so that the appropriate workflow can be defined.

Corporate buyers do not search for 'electronic waste disposal' — they need to resolve an event: a decommissioning, a data risk, a backlog of returns, an audit on the horizon. Each solution below addresses one of those events, with its own scope, process and documentation.

When the problem involves equipment and data

  • Decommissioned IT assets — Estate refresh, end of contract and site closure — with inventory and chain of custody.
  • Secure data sanitisation — Logical erasure with a per-media report — for leasing, reuse and donation.
  • Physical destruction of data and media — Permanent destruction under custody — for policies that rule out reuse.
  • Data centre decommissioning — From the rack to the handed-over premises, run as a project with a timetable.
  • Corporate IT disposal — The general entry point for the IT estates of companies and institutions.

title: Data destruction and sanitisation: which path does your case require?
custom_excerpt: Two distinct services for end-of-life data — logical sanitisation (the equipment survives) and physical destruction (media and data are destroyed together) — understand which applies and request an assessment.

meta_description: Logical sanitisation or physical destruction? Understand which data treatment your case requires — and request a technical assessment with per-media reporting.
html:
Two paths — and mixing them up is a technical error

Every piece of equipment with data media that leaves the organisation demands a decision: sanitise (remove the data logically and preserve the equipment) or physically destroy (render the media permanently unusable). They are services with different methods, deliverables and uses — and treating them as the same thing produces an imprecise offering and fragile evidence.

Secure data sanitisation — when the equipment needs to survive

Lease returns, internal reuse and donation: the data is eliminated, the machine remains usable. Documented method and a per-media report. When sanitisation is not technically applicable (damaged media, encryption without the key), you are informed and the case proceeds to physical destruction.

See the secure data sanitisation service →

Physical destruction of data and media — when policy does not allow reuse

HDDs, SSDs, tapes and media rendered permanently unusable, with chain of custody through to destruction, a per-media record and documented destination of the resulting waste.

See the physical destruction of data and media service →

Which one should you choose?

  • Will the machine be returned, donated or reused? → Sanitisation.
  • Does policy prohibit reuse, or does an audit require the media to be rendered unusable? → Physical destruction.
  • Is the media damaged, or encrypted without the key? → Physical destruction.
  • Mixed estate or technical doubt? → The assessment decides media by media — part may be sanitised, part destroyed, all with records.

On both paths, the same standard of proof

Inventory, chain of custody, a per-media treatment record and, when the operation includes equipment disposal, the applicable MTR and CDF. See how the evidence is built in documentation and traceability — and Ecobraz's public records in public evidence.

Start with the technical assessment

Describe the media, the volume and the requirements of your case. The team will come back with the applicable path, the scope and the report template.

The type of material, its origin, the transport, the treatment and the waste generator's requirements determine which records apply. Documentation should be defined before the operation and issued consistently with the contracted service.

Proper management of electronic waste in Osasco is a growing necessity, driven by the rising consumption of electronic equipment and the environmental impact of incorrect disposal. Collection and Final Disposal Processes for E-Waste in Osasco

The most efficient route for e-waste collection in Osasco involves authorised collection points and reverse logistics operations, which direct waste to appropriate treatment and help prevent contamination of soil, water and air. These processes rely on sorting, dismantling and recycling capabilities, promoting the recovery of reusable materials and preventing improper disposal.

To carry out collection properly, we recommend the specialised service available for scheduling at e-waste collection in Osasco, supporting environmental compliance and the security of the procedure.

Secure Disposal of Data Storage Devices

Devices that store information, such as hard disk drives (HDDs) and other media, require a rigorous secure-disposal process. Responsibilities and Good Practice for Companies and Public Bodies

Public and private organisations in Osasco should implement internal selective-collection programmes and encourage the correct return of electronic equipment at the end of its life cycle. Adopting these practices reduces environmental impact, addresses legal obligations and promotes sustainability.

Environmental and Social Benefits of Recycling Electronic Equipment

The correct recycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment contributes to the conservation of natural resources, the reduction of pollution and the creation of jobs across authorised recycling chains. This movement is aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and national environmental policies.

Conclusion

E-waste collection in Osasco must observe technical and legal standards, promoting environmental sustainability and information security. Scheduling a specialised, documented service is essential so that waste is handled in an environmentally appropriate and technologically secure manner.

The proper disposal of fridges prevents soil and water contamination by refrigerants and heavy metals. It also promotes the recycling of recoverable components, reducing the consumption of natural resources. Complying with current legislation protects the environment and contributes to the circular economy.

Technical data such as IP address, browser and access logs may be processed for security, diagnostics and measurement.

3. Purposes

  • Assessing the request and verifying whether the collection is feasible;
  • Making contact, preparing a proposal and organising the operation;
  • Recording the enquiry in our sales system;
  • Preventing abuse, fraud and security failures;
  • Measuring the performance of the website and of campaigns;
  • Sending marketing communications only where authorisation or another applicable legal basis exists.

4. Sharing and processors

Data may be processed by suppliers required for hosting, security, customer service, CRM, automation and communication. The form feeds requests into Ploomes. Where the data subject ticks the communications option, their contact details may also be sent to E-goi. These suppliers receive only the data necessary for their respective purposes.

5. Legal bases and consent

Processing may take place for preliminary procedures related to the request, performance of a contract, compliance with obligations, the regular exercise of rights, assessed legitimate interest and consent, depending on the purpose. Marketing authorisation is optional and may be withdrawn.

6. Retention

Data are kept for the period necessary for handling the enquiry, the commercial relationship, legal obligations, dispute prevention and the protection of rights. They may subsequently be erased, anonymised or retained where an applicable legal ground exists.

7. Data subject rights

Data subjects may request confirmation of processing, access, rectification, information about data sharing and the other rights provided for in applicable legislation. Requests must allow the identity of the requester to be verified securely.

8. Cookies and metrics

The website may use essential technologies and measurement tools for operation, security and performance analysis. Browser settings can limit cookies, although some functions may be affected.

9. Security and updates

Ecobraz adopts technical and administrative measures proportionate to the processing. No environment is entirely immune to incidents. This policy may be updated to reflect operational, legal or technological changes, with the date of the current version indicated.

Cookies, measurement and consent

What we use: the website uses Google Analytics 4 to measure visits, traffic sources and interactions (such as button clicks and form submissions). These measurements use Google cookies and identifiers (tag G-Y1ERW8GNPR).

Consent mode: we apply Google Consent Mode v2. For visitors from the European Union, the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, measurement starts switched off and is only enabled after acceptance in the cookie banner. For all other visitors, measurement starts enabled, with the option to decline available in the same banner.

Your choice: your decision (accept or decline) is stored in your browser and applies to subsequent visits. You can change it at any time via the Cookie preferences link in the footer of any page.

Heatmaps (Microsoft Clarity): we use Microsoft Clarity to understand how visitors use the website (the areas most clicked, how far pages are scrolled and anonymised session replays), with the aim of improving the experience. Text typed into form fields is masked by default and the tool respects the same cookie-banner choice described above.

Ad conversion measurement: when the collection form is submitted, the e-mail address and telephone number provided may be transmitted to Google in encrypted (hashed) form, solely to identify which advert originated the enquiry (Google Ads enhanced conversions). This transfer respects the same cookie-banner choice described above: where cookies are declined, these data are not used.

What we do not do: we do not sell browsing data and we do not send marketing communications without your specific consent, which is given via a separate, optional checkbox when the request is submitted.

html:
Cut-off date for this page: 14 July 2026. Each item below presents the fact, the official source and the exact limit of what the evidence proves. Nothing beyond the verifiable is claimed.

Principles adopted

Authority does not come from absolute promises. It depends on clear scope, identified responsibilities, consistent records and documents that represent the materials, the stages and the service actually performed. What exists is shown; what is pending is flagged; what cannot be proven is never turned into a promise.

Public records and listings for Ecobraz

European Union — good practice listed on the ECESP

Ecobraz's Adopt a Neighbourhood programme (Adote um Bairro) is listed as a good practice on the European Circular Economy Stakeholder Platform (ECESP), a joint initiative of the European Commission and the EESC. Listing is visibility, not endorsement. See the official listing. What this does not mean: approval, certification or any seal of the European Union.

United Nations — profile in the civil society database

Ecobraz is listed in the United Nations iCSO database — the UN's civil society participation database — under code 708794; a listing, not an endorsement. See the official record. What this does not mean: affiliation, accreditation or partnership with the UN, nor ECOSOC consultative status.

World Bank — citation in an infoDev report

Ecobraz was cited in an infoDev/World Bank Group study on models and scaling conditions in green sectors (“Innovations for Scaling Green Sectors”, 2017), in the section dedicated to electronic waste management. See the report. What this does not mean: recommendation, certification, funding or partnership with the World Bank.

Brazil — founded in 2011

Ecobraz is a Brazilian civil society organisation (CNPJ 14.197.457/0001-42), founded in 2011.

Chronology note: Ecobraz was founded in 2011 (15 years of operation in 2026). External references to “16 years of experience” — such as the listing on the European platform — refer to the founding team's track record in the sector prior to the organisation's formal constitution.

CETEM — REMINARE operators register

Ecobraz/Emigre declares that it is included in the register of REMINARE operators maintained by the Centre for Mineral Technology (CETEM). Direct public verification pending: the official page renders the list dynamically and may not show the name in a plain-text reading; until a directly verifiable record is published, this evidence is classified as pending. See the listing. What this does not mean: a licence, certification or official approval.

Technical publications by Marcio Villanova

Marcio Villanova, CEO of Ecobraz and founder of Villanova ESG, maintains a public author identity under ORCID 0009-0001-8072-6287 and technical reports with persistent identifiers (DOIs) deposited on Zenodo, covering supplier evidence, financial risk, buyer-readiness, Brazil–Europe supply chains and corporate IT disposal. The 7 publications:

  • The EU-Brazil Supplier Evidence Gap: Operational Traceability, Buyer-Readable Documentation and Regulatory Defensibility — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20293223
  • EU-Brazil Supplier Evidence Gap: A Technical Report on Regulatory Defensibility, Buyer-Readiness and Audit-Grade Documentation — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20317248
  • Audit-Grade Evidence as a Financial Risk Control in EU-Brazil Supply Chains — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20319388

  • The Evidence Compression Risk: Why EU Regulatory Simplification May Increase Supplier Pressure for Brazilian Exporters — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20371672

Note: the first report also carries the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20293222, which aggregates all versions and does not constitute an additional publication. There are 7 distinct publications.

The technical work of Marcio Villanova and Villanova ESG has public entries on the European Circular Economy Stakeholder Platform, including the circular supply chain evidence toolkit for non-EU suppliers and the position paper on the EU–Mercosur agreement. These listings are visibility, not endorsement. Note: ORCID is a self-managed persistent identifier, and deposit on Zenodo does not constitute peer review or institutional endorsement.

Aggregate operational figures (collections, clients, total tonnes) will be published only after reconciliation with primary records, together with the methodology and a cut-off date.

Confirm who performs each stage, which materials are accepted, where each party's responsibility ends, which evidence will be delivered and which exceptions may prevent the operation. An inventory, a collection record, a chain of custody, a processing report and proofs of final destination serve different purposes — the requirement should be stated before the proposal.

html:
When a one-off collection is not enough

Organisations with multiple sites, ongoing asset refresh cycles or frequent maintenance need a repeatable process. Recurring collections reduce accumulation, standardise requests and improve visibility over materials and documents.

Programme elements

  • Sites and regions covered;
  • Accepted material categories;
  • Minimum volume, frequency or collection trigger;
  • Local and central points of contact;
  • Packaging and labelling standards;
  • Data, inventory and documentation requirements;
  • Reports and indicators consistent with the scope.

Operating models

The programme can be based on a calendar, accumulated volume or per-site requests. The design depends on geographic spread, predictability, criticality and temporary storage capacity.

Who it is for

Retail chains, education networks, hospitals and clinics, manufacturing sites, offices, multi-tenant buildings, repair and service centres, data centres and organisations with multiple points of generation.

Frequently asked questions

Is a contract required?

Commercial and documentation terms are defined according to the programme and the expected recurrence.

Do all sites need to generate the same volume?

No. The plan can group locations and set different criteria, provided the flow remains operationally viable.

Contact us to design a recurring collection programme

html:
Reverse logistics is an operation, not just transport

An efficient flow connects generation, storage, consolidation, collection, checking, treatment and evidence. The design should take into account materials, risks, distances, frequency, responsibilities and the data needed for management.

Possible scopes

  • Pick-up at head office, branches, shops or customer sites;
  • Regional consolidation of small volumes;
  • Internal campaigns or permanent programmes;
  • Decommissioning of IT assets;
  • Flows for technical repair, exchanges and post-consumer returns;
  • Integration with inventory and operational records.

Decisions before roll-out

  1. Define which materials the programme covers.
  2. Map generation points and expected volumes.
  3. Establish packaging, labelling and responsible staff.
  4. Choose the collection trigger and the level of traceability.
  5. Define how exceptions and non-conforming items are handled.

Useful indicators

Volume by category and site, time to collection, non-conformity rate, reconciled assets and completed documents help keep the process under control. Indicators should reflect data that is actually collected.

Data centre decommissioning demands planning

Servers, storage arrays, switches, routers, racks and power units concentrate weight, data and operational dependencies. Collection must be planned around the inventory, the shutdown window, site access and the security controls required.

Assets covered

  • Rack, tower and blade servers;
  • Storage arrays, appliances, tape libraries and tapes;
  • Switches, routers, firewalls and telecoms equipment;
  • Racks, rails, PDUs, UPS units and cabling;
  • HDDs, SSDs and other removable media.

Critical points of the operation

  • Weight, dimensions, lifts, loading docks and access restrictions;
  • Asset identification and reconciliation against the inventory;
  • Segregation of media and definition of the data treatment;
  • Chain of custody and named owners for each handover;
  • A schedule compatible with business continuity.

Frequently asked questions

Does the team dismantle racks and infrastructure?

This requirement should be described for technical assessment. The proposal sets out what is and is not included.

Can media be tracked separately?

Yes, when provided for in the scope. State the quantity, the technology and the evidence required.

title: Technical Publications
custom_excerpt: Original technical reports by Ecobraz Emigre on governance, evidence and the destination of post-use electronics, each with a persistent DOI on the Zenodo repository.
meta_title: Technical Publications with DOIs | Ecobraz
meta_description: Technical reports by Ecobraz Emigre on governance, evidence and electronics reverse logistics, published on the Zenodo repository with persistent DOIs.
html:
Ecobraz Emigre publishes original technical reports on the governance, evidence and final destination of post-use electrical and electronic assets. Each report is deposited on Zenodo — an open research repository operated by CERN — and receives a DOI (Digital Object Identifier), a persistent identifier that ensures the document can be located and cited in a stable way, today and in the future.

These are technical and conceptual works authored by Marcio Villanova (ORCID 0009-0001-8072-6287), version 1.0, not submitted to peer review. They do not replace the legal, environmental or technical assessment applicable to each specific case — and it is precisely this transparency about scope and limits that also guides our operation.

Published reports

1. Post-Use Electrical and Electronic Assets as Corporate Risk: Environmental, Asset and Information Governance

Proposes a conceptual matrix of post-use exposure across the environmental, asset, information and evidential dimensions — distinguishing retirement from use, asset write-off, physical removal, data treatment and environmental destination as separate events, each with its own responsible parties and its own evidence.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Ativos Eletroeletrônicos Pós-Uso como Risco Corporativo: Governança Ambiental, Patrimonial e Informacional. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21397950 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

2. Asset Write-Off Does Not End the Risk: Responsibilities and Evidence in IT Asset Decommissioning

Shows why a write-off in the fixed-asset register does not, on its own, prove physical removal, transfer of custody, data treatment or environmental destination — and proposes the Post-Use Closure Vector to track each closure state separately.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. A Baixa Patrimonial Não Encerra o Risco: Responsabilidades e Evidências no Descomissionamento de Ativos de TI. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398130 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

3. Residual Data Risk in Decommissioned Equipment: Media Governance, Sanitisation and Accountability

Relates the duties under the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law), the guidance issued by the ANPD and the NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 technical reference, and proposes the Residual Information Risk Matrix to decide the appropriate treatment for each type of media — without assuming that a single technique suits every case.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Risco Residual de Dados em Equipamentos Desativados: Governança de Mídias, Sanitização e Prestação de Contas. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398306 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

4. Chain of Custody for Electronic Waste: Integrity, Continuity and Traceability of Evidence

A conceptual chain-of-custody architecture — the ability to maintain a reconstructable link between object, custodian, event, time and evidence — with terminology grounded in ISO 22095 and an analysis of the distinct documentary functions of the MTR (waste transport manifest) and the CDF (final destination certificate).

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Cadeia de Custódia de Resíduos Eletroeletrônicos: Integridade, Continuidade e Rastreabilidade da Evidência. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398390 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

5. From Collection to Final Destination: What Each Stage Can Support — and What It Cannot

Starts from the principle of minimal assertion: a request is not a booking, a booking is not a collection, a collection is not receipt, and an MTR is not a CDF. Proposes the Evidential Scope Matrix by Stage, linking each record to the fact it actually supports.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Da Coleta à Destinação: O que Cada Etapa Pode Sustentar - e o que Não Sustenta. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398750 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

6. Evidence of Environmental Destination: Scope and Limits of Documents, Records and Certificates in Isolation

Examines what collection, transport, receipt and destination documents can prove on their own, and proposes the Evidential Sufficiency Matrix — seven qualitative tests to assess the issuer, object, scope and consistency of each record.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Evidência de Destinação Ambiental: Alcance e Limites de Documentos, Registros e Certificados Isolados. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398814 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

7. Qualifying Reverse Logistics Providers: Risk-Based Due Diligence for Procurement, Compliance and Audit

A risk-based due diligence framework for qualifying and monitoring providers of removal, transport, treatment and final destination — showing why a licence, a price, a contract or a certificate in isolation does not demonstrate all the competence required for a specific scope.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Qualificação de Prestadores de Logística Reversa: Due Diligence Baseada em Risco para Compras, Compliance e Auditoria. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398879 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

8. Multi-Site Reverse Logistics: Controls for Distributed Corporate Operations

Governance for operations that remove electrical and electronic assets from multiple sites, cities or states: how to balance corporate standards with local conditions while keeping inventories, providers and evidence reconcilable with one another.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Logística Reversa Multissite: Controles para Operações Corporativas Distribuídas. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398926 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

9. Non-Conformities in the Destination of Electronics: A Taxonomy for Audit and Corporate Control

A taxonomy with six finding states for recording and handling documentary discrepancies without going beyond the available facts — separating immediate correction, root-cause analysis, corrective action and closure verification.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Não Conformidades na Destinação de Eletroeletrônicos: Uma Taxonomia para Auditoria e Controle Corporativo. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21398989 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

10. Indicators Without Evidence: The Limits of Weight, Volume and Recycling Percentages in Corporate Accountability

Examines why weight, volume and percentages can appear precise and still be insufficient for accountability purposes. Proposes the Waste Indicator Identity Sheet and distinguishes measured, calculated, estimated, declared and verified values.

How to cite: VILLANOVA, Marcio. Indicadores sem Evidência: Limites de Peso, Volume e Percentuais de Reciclagem na Prestação de Contas Corporativa. Zenodo, 2026. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21399040 (open-access PDF, in Portuguese).

Use and reproduction

The PDFs are available in open access on each DOI page. To cite them in papers, proposals or internal policies, use the format indicated for each report. Questions about the topics covered can be sent by email to contato@ecobraz.org.br or through the Ecobraz channels.

See also the public evidence of our operation and the author profile of Marcio Villanova.

title: Telecoms equipment disposal
custom_excerpt: Collection of exchanges, switches, routers, radios, antennas, telephony and telecommunications infrastructure, with inventory and logistics planned to the project.
meta_title: Telecoms equipment disposal | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request an assessment for the collection of exchanges, switches, routers, radios, antennas, telephony, power supplies and telecommunications assets.
html:
Networks and telecommunications combine assets, data and infrastructure

Exchanges, switches, routers, radios and transmission equipment may hold configurations, credentials, modules, batteries and components installed in controlled-access locations. Removal must take account of inventory, shutdown, dismantling and handling.

Assets for assessment

  • Telephone exchanges, IP handsets and gateways;
  • Switches, routers, firewalls and appliances;
  • Radios, antennas, repeaters and transmission equipment;
  • Racks, patch panels, power supplies, modules and cabling;
  • Equipment from carriers, service providers, data centres and corporate networks.

Planning the collection

Tell us the models, quantities, location, weight, installation height, any dismantling required and whether sensitive data or configurations are present. Work at height, technical areas and energised sites call for a specific assessment.

Frequently asked questions

Does the collection include removing installed antennas?

Not automatically. Dismantling, work at height and technical access must be set out in the scope and may require specialised resources.

Can assets be inventoried by serial number?

Yes, when requested and approved before the operation.

Contact us to request a telecoms assessment

title: Old TV and monitor disposal
custom_excerpt: Request an assessment for the disposal of CRT, LCD, LED and plasma televisions, monitors and audio-visual equipment.
meta_title: Where to dispose of old TVs and monitors | Ecobraz
meta_description: Assessment for the disposal of CRT, LCD, LED and plasma TVs and monitors. Tell us the type, size, quantity and address, and send photos.
html:
Old TVs should not go into general waste

CRT, LCD, LED and plasma televisions contain glass, circuit boards, cables, metals and components that require proper end-of-life treatment. Broken screens also call for additional care during packaging and transport.

Items that can be included in a request

  • CRT, LCD, LED and plasma TVs;
  • Computer monitors and professional displays;
  • Projectors, audio systems and video equipment;
  • Remote controls, cables, power supplies and accessories.

What to tell us

Describe the screen technology, approximate size, quantity, condition of the screens, address and access conditions. Do not break up or dismantle the equipment to reduce its volume.

Frequently asked questions

Do you collect CRT televisions?

Each item can be assessed according to location, quantity, condition and logistics.

Can a broken screen be collected?

Let us know about this condition and send photos. Packaging must protect people and prevent fragments from dispersing.

Contact us to request a TV and monitor assessment

title: Washing machine disposal
custom_excerpt: Assessment-based collection of washing machines, tumble dryers, twin tubs and dishwashers, taking address, weight and access into account.
meta_title: Old washing machine disposal and collection | Ecobraz
meta_description: Request an assessment for washing machine, tumble dryer or twin-tub disposal. Provide the postcode, photos, access details, quantity and condition.
html:
Where to dispose of an old or broken washing machine

Washing machines combine a metal frame, motor, circuit boards, cables, plastics and components that can be recovered or routed for treatment. Because they are heavy and bulky, removal needs to take the route to the vehicle into account.

Equipment that can be assessed

  • Automatic and semi-automatic washing machines;
  • Tumble dryers, twin tubs and spin dryers;
  • Dishwashers and laundry equipment;
  • Residential, commercial and industrial machines.

Prepare the information

Send photos, the approximate model, quantity, address, floor, lift, stairs and any time restrictions. Also let us know whether the equipment is disconnected and drained of water.

Frequently asked questions

Do you collect a single machine?

Feasibility depends on the location and the operational route. Contact us so we can assess the alternative available for your case.

Does an industrial machine follow the same process?

Industrial equipment requires weight, dimensions, rating plate, access conditions and any handling resources to be confirmed before a proposal is issued.

Contact us about washing machine collection

title: White goods and household appliance disposal
custom_excerpt: Request an assessment for the collection of fridges, washing machines, microwaves, televisions and other household appliances, subject to location, volume and access.
meta_title: White goods and household appliance disposal | Ecobraz
meta_description: Assessment for disposing of fridges, washing machines, microwaves, TVs and appliances. Share your address, access details, quantity and condition.
html:
Where to dispose of fridges, washing machines and household appliances

Old household appliances are bulky and may contain circuit boards, motors, cables, oils, gases, batteries and other components. The collection option available depends on the address, the volume, the condition of the equipment and the handling conditions on site.

Items that can be assessed

  • Fridges, freezers, minibars and water dispensers;
  • Washing machines, tumble dryers and dishwashers;
  • Microwaves, ovens and small appliances;
  • Televisions, audio equipment and household electronics;
  • Air-conditioning and climate-control equipment, subject to specific analysis.

What to include in your request

Provide the quantity, photos, address, floor, lift access, stairs, parking and whether the equipment is intact. Do not remove gases, compressors or components yourself.

Frequently asked questions

Is collection free of charge?

There is no single answer. Feasibility and costs vary according to location, item, quantity, access and the operation required.

Do you collect broken washing machines?

Send us the address and photos so we can check which option is available in your region.

Contact us to arrange appliance collection
